summary.title: The Product-Minded Software Engineer
summary.one_liner: Product-minded engineers care about the "why" behind product decisions, and this article lays out 9 traits they share and tips for building that habit.
takeaways: Product-minded engineers question specs, propose alternatives, and understand the business, users, and data behind them.
They weigh product and engineering tradeoffs together, such as suggesting a different feature with similar impact but much less effort.
They handle edge cases pragmatically by weighing impact against effort, and look for non-engineering fixes like customer support.
They validate ideas early with hallway tests, demos to the PM, or bug bashes, and follow up on real-world results after launch.
To grow this skill: learn how the company makes money, build a relationship with your PM, join user research and support, and ask the PM for feedback.
summary.summary: Gergely Orosz describes product-minded software engineers, developers who are deeply interested in the product, its users, and the business behind it. The article draws on his observations and on quotes from Sherif Mansour (Atlassian PM) and Jean-Michel Lemieux (Shopify engineering head). It lists nine traits, including proactive product ideas, curiosity about "why", strong communication with non-engineers, combined product and engineering tradeoffs, pragmatic edge-case handling, quick validation, and end-to-end ownership through post-launch results. It closes with practical tips for engineers who want to grow these habits.
